entities.summary: Yuri Khanon is a pen name of Yuri Feliksovich Soloviev-Savoyarov, a Russian composer. Prior to 1993, he wrote under a pen name Yuri Khanin, but later transformed it into Yuri Khanon, spelling it in a pre-1918 Russian style as ХанонЪ. Khanon was born on June 16, 1965, in Leningrad. In 1988, he became a laureate of the European Film Awards, and in 1989, he won the Nika Award, a Russian cinematographic award. Due to his numerous concerts throughout Russia, as well as to TV and cinema appearances, Khanon reached the peak of his popularity in 1988–1992, but in 1993, decided to stop performing in public.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a renowned Russian composer, Yuri Khanon's popularity peaked in 1988-1992 with numerous concerts and TV appearances, leading to him becoming a laureate of the European Film Awards in 1988 and winning the Nika Award in 1989. His decision to stop performing in public in 1993 marked a significant shift in his career.
